items.stem: A RAG system retrieves the right document in its top 20 but the answer still misses it. Adding which component most directly raises the chance the key passage is actually used?

options.text: A reranker that reorders the 20 candidates so the most relevant passage lands in the top few the model reads
options.rationale: Correct: reranking raises precision of the small set the model actually consumes.
A better first-stage embedder helps recall but does not reorder the shortlist the model reads.
Randomness does not improve which passage is used.
That widens results and can lower precision.

items.explanation: Correct: reranking raises precision of the small set the model actually consumes.

items.stem: Which TWO metrics specifically measure retrieval quality (not generation quality)? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: recall@k measures whether relevant passages appear in the top k retrieved.
Correct: MRR measures how highly the first relevant passage is ranked.
Groundedness measures the generated answer against its sources, not retrieval.
Fluency is a generation-side property, not retrieval quality.

items.stem: Why can hybrid search (keyword plus vector) outperform pure vector search?

options.text: Keyword matching catches exact terms, codes and rare tokens that embeddings may blur, while vectors catch paraphrase
options.rationale: Correct: the two methods are complementary, improving recall across query types.

options.text: It eliminates the need for any index

options.rationale: Running two retrievers usually adds latency.

options.text: It removes the need for a generation model
options.rationale: Generation is still required to produce the answer.
